title: Banking System Reform (Separation of Banks) Bill 2019
short_title: Banking System Reform (Separation of Banks) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would separate deposit-taking banks from non-bank businesses and restrict banks’ activities, including proprietary trading, derivatives dealings and involvement in managed investment schemes.
Banks would generally have 24 months to end prohibited affiliations, with regulated extensions possible, while core services such as deposits, lending and payments would be permitted.
A new parliamentary committee would oversee the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority, and deposit protection would be limited to accounts at banks avoiding prohibited activities.
changes: Non-banks would be prohibited from accepting deposits of the specified kind.
People holding specified roles in prohibited affiliates generally could not hold equivalent positions in banks.
New prudential standards would require parliamentary approval.
summary.affected: Banks, their non-bank affiliates and officers, depositors and the Australian Prudential Regulation Authority are affected.
